subject: Evidence package request: backup erasure & certification for upcoming audit
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: proof of backup deletion propagation for legal hold item

Hi Vanessa,

We have an upcoming regulatory audit (May 10) and the auditors have requested evidence that when a governed record is deleted under a legal hold, the deletion propagates through active backups and DR copies within a defined SLA. Specifically they want:

- A timeline showing when the original record was deleted from the primary service, and when the deletion was removed from backups/replicas (or confirmation it was never snapshotted after the hold).
- Export of expunge/delete logs and any snapshot manifests showing tombstone/expiry events.
- A short explainer of how Redwood ensures deletion does not get reintroduced by DR restores or replica replay.

Can you confirm whether we can get this evidence by May 3? Also let me know if you need a signed NDA or a specific template for the audit packet.

Thanks,
Sarah

Subject: Re: Request: proof of backup deletion propagation for legal hold item

Vanessa / SooJin —

Summary of technical facts (for inclusion in the packet):

1) Deletion model: when a customer issues a delete for a governed object under legal hold, the object is tombstoned in the primary store immediately (logical delete). Tombstones are propagated to the distributed metadata tier and to the snapshot manifest service.

2) Backup/DR propagation: our snapshot pipeline writes manifests that reference object IDs and snapshot timestamps. Tombstone entries are included as metadata flags; the expunge worker evaluates retention windows and final expunge actions. Expunge is performed in two phases: mark-for-expire (ID moved to expunge queue) and final-expunge (object data removed from object store and manifests updated).

3) Typical timing: for protected/legal-hold deletes we stop automatic expunge and escalate to legal review. For standard deletes (no hold) the mark-for-expire -> final-expunge window is typically 48–72 hours for nearline replicas, and up to 7 days for offsite archival tiers. For the Acme case (you provided case id ACME-2026-LH-42), per retention override the expunge was gated until legal clearance.

4) Evidence artifacts we can provide:
- snapshot-manifest-20270420-20270428.jsonl (manifest records with tombstone flags)
- backup-expunge-log-20270428.csv (worker events with timestamps and op codes)
- object-hash-report-20270428.txt (SHA256 of final-manifest exports)
- audit-statement-ops-20270429.pdf (ops readout of sequence numbers and replica lag)

5) Restore safety: restores use manifest-anchored reconciliation. Any object absent from the latest manifest (or marked expunged) is excluded from restore bundles. We also maintain a denylist of object IDs that must not be re-ingested during restore windows; restores consult that list as part of consistency checks.

I'll attach the logs and the hash report; the ops PDF is draft and should be reviewed by Legal before external delivery.

Attachments (attached to this thread): backup-expunge-log-20270428.csv, snapshot-manifest-20270420-20270428.jsonl (redacted), object-hash-report-20270428.txt

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Final: audit evidence package — backup deletion & propagation (Acme Case ACME-2026-LH-42)

Hi Sarah — attaching the evidence package for Acme's auditors. See attachments and notes below.

Attachments included:
- acme_deletion_timeline_20270429.pdf (high-level timeline + certification statement)
- backup-expunge-log-20270428.csv (worker-level events; redacted PII)
- snapshot-hash-report.txt (SHA256 of exported manifests)

Key points for auditors (summary):
- The governed object was tombstoned in the primary on 2027-04-20T14:32:05Z.
- Manifest entries show tombstone flags propagated to snapshot manifests between 2027-04-20 and 2027-04-21 (manifest sequence numbers 1092–1101).
- No final expunge occurred while legal hold was active; expunge was gated by legal review (ACME-2026-LH-42). Final expunge was actioned only after documented legal authorization on 2027-04-26, and worker logs show final-expunge completed on 2027-04-28T03:11:22Z across primary and nearline replicas.
- Our restore process consults manifest state and a denylist; we include a cryptographic hash bundle and signed timestamp for the exported manifests to show integrity.

Links for your auditors: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Acme/backup-erasure-evidence-2027-04-29 (contains the packet and SHA bundle)

If the auditors need notarized timestamps, we can request an independently signed timestamp from our time-stamping service — let me know and we'll add that.

Please confirm receipt and whether you want anything redacted. SooJin (Legal) is on copy and will advise on redactions for any externally shared manifests.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
